change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admin check uses && with isTeamOwner, so only owners pass
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already returns the membership for role ADMIN or OWNER (`packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284`), and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER (`:286-295`). Joining them with `&&` leaves owners as the only team members who pass. Team admins who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, although the variable name says admin or owner. Use `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`, which already covers owners.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive on the guest side, and base-email handling is skipped
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is compared as submitted. If `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` contains `spam@x.com`, then `Spam@X.com` passes. `handleNewBooking.ts:736-743` lowercases both sides and uses `extractBaseEmail`, so `+alias` variants are caught there. This path skips that, which lets someone get a blocked address onto a booking and trigger an email to it. Lowercase the guest and reuse `extractBaseEmail`, as `handleNewBooking.ts:742` does.

findings.title: Server does not dedupe the submitted guests or compare existing attendees case-insensitively
findings.body: The unique-email rule is enforced only in the dialog (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29`). `addGuests.schema.ts:5` accepts any array. A direct tRPC call with `[a@x.com, a@x.com]` passes the filter on lines 74-78, because it only compares against existing attendees. `createMany` then inserts two attendee rows for the same address. `A@x.com` also passes against an existing `a@x.com`. Dedupe `uniqueGuests` after lowercasing and compare case-insensitively against existing attendees. Consider adding `.min(1)` and a `.max()` to the schema, since each guest triggers an outbound email.

findings.title: Attendees are committed before the fallible steps, with no recovery path
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update` (lines 92-106) persists the new attendees. After that come `getTranslation`, `getUsersCredentials`, `new EventManager` and `updateCalendarAttendees` (lines 108-165), none of them in a try/catch. If one throws, the client gets a 500 and an error toast, but the guests are already stored and no emails go out. Retrying then hits `uniqueGuests.length === 0` (line 80) and shows 'Emails must be unique and valid', so the user has no way to get the guests notified. Siblings are not a clean template here: `editLocation.handler.ts:116` writes to the DB only after the calendar update succeeds. Move the DB write after the calendar update, or handle the failure explicitly. Also check what `updateCalendarAttendees` returns: its result is ignored, and it returns early without error when `booking.references` is empty (`EventManager.ts:597-600`).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's host/attendee email-disable settings
findings.body: The sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` (`email-manager.ts:495-524`) takes `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host emails when `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` is true and attendee emails when `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` is true. The new function always emails the organizer and every attendee. The handler never passes `booking.eventType.metadata`. Event types that disabled these emails will still send them, to the new guests, existing attendees and the organizer. Accept the metadata and apply the same two guards.

findings.title: New-guest detection uses the raw request list, and team-member branch is dead for this caller
findings.body: The handler passes `guests` (the raw input, line 168 of `addGuests.handler.ts`), not `uniqueGuests`. An existing attendee who was re-submitted in the input gets the 'scheduled' email, as if they were new, instead of the 'guests added' email. Also, `evt` in the handler never sets `team`, so the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop on lines 531-537 never runs here. For team events, the other hosts are not notified. Pass `uniqueGuests` and either populate `team` or drop the loop.

findings.title: Invalid-email banner is never cleared on success or when the dialog is dismissed otherwise
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation (line 56). It is reset only in the Cancel button handler (line 91). It is not reset in `onSuccess` (lines 36-41), nor when the dialog closes via Esc or overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61), nor when the user edits the inputs. So after one invalid attempt, then a corrected and successful add, the next open of the dialog shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner immediately. The same Esc or overlay close leaves stale `multiEmailValue`. Reset both states in one close handler used by all paths.

findings.title: onError message is always truthy, so the fallback key is dead and the toast is noisy
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back, and the `unable_to_add_guests` string added to `common.json` is never used. The toast shows `NOT_FOUND: booking_not_found` style text, and zod failures put raw JSON into `t()`. Show `t(err.message)` only for the known keys the handler throws, and otherwise `t("unable_to_add_guests")`. Separately, with zero rows, `handleAdd` returns silently (line 49-51): after removing every row, clicking Add does nothing.

findings.title: Schema is rebuilt on every render and duplicates the server schema
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is created inside the component body each render, and it shadows the name of the server schema in `addGuests.schema.ts`. Move it to module scope. Use `.toLowerCase()` for the duplicate comparison so it matches what the server should do.

findings.title: Copy of the form-builder MultiEmail; imports the package barrel from inside the package; hardcoded tooltip
findings.body: `packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:233-234` already has a `MultiEmail` factory marked 'TODO: Make it a ui component'. This PR adds a copy and does not replace the original, so there are now two implementations. The other components in `packages/ui/form` import relatively (`AddressInput.tsx:4`, `fields.tsx:11`), but this file imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, which is a circular import through `index.tsx`. The tooltip text 'Remove email' (line 46) is not translated. `label htmlFor="emails"` (line 21) points at no element id, and `key={index}` (line 26) is risky when rows are removed from the middle.

findings.title: No check of booking status, end time, or seat configuration before adding attendees
findings.body: The handler loads the booking by id and checks only the caller's relation. It does not check whether the booking is cancelled or rejected, or whether it is already past. It also does not check `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`: attendees are inserted directly, with no seat references and no seat-count check. The UI shows the action only under `bookedActions` (`BookingListItem.tsx:214-231`), which is client-side only. Is adding guests meant to be allowed in these states? If not, the handler should reject them.

findings.title: No tests for a new permission-gated mutation
findings.body: The PR adds no unit or e2e tests. The authorization branches (organizer, attendee, team admin or owner), the blacklist and dedupe filtering, and the email recipient split (new guest versus existing attendee) are all untested. The `&&` bug on line 48 is the kind of defect a permission test would catch.

contracts.action: User submits the Add guests dialog, which calls trpc viewer.bookings.addGuests
contracts.equivalent_path: editLocation via bookingsProcedure (`_router.tsx:62`), which restricts to the organizer or collective-event users before the handler runs (`util.ts:19-65`).
contracts.before_after: The new route uses `authedProcedure`, with an inline permission check in the handler: organizer, any attendee matched by email, or team owner (the admin check is broken by the `&&` on line 48). editLocation writes to the DB only after the calendar update succeeds (`editLocation.handler.ts:107-126`). addGuests writes attendees first (`addGuests.handler.ts:92-106`), then updates the calendar (line 165), then sends emails.
contracts.visible_effect: On success: a toast, the dialog closes, and `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` refreshes the list, so the new attendees appear. The `isInvalidEmail` state is not reset on success.
contracts.failure_mode: If anything after the DB write throws, the client gets an error toast, but the guests are already saved. A retry returns 'Emails must be unique and valid' and no emails are ever sent. Errors are shown as `CODE: message`.

contracts.action: sendAddGuestsEmails sends email to the organizer, any team members, and every attendee
contracts.equivalent_path: sendLocationChangeEmails (`email-manager.ts:495-524`), which honours eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail from event type metadata.
contracts.before_after: The sibling checks the metadata before sending to hosts and attendees. The new function never does, and the handler does not pass the metadata. Team-member emails depend on `calendarEvent.team`, which the handler's `evt` never sets.
contracts.visible_effect: New guests receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail. Existing attendees and the organizer receive the new 'guests added' emails. Email is sent even for event types that disabled it.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors from `sendAddGuestsEmails` are caught and only `console.log`ged (`addGuests.handler.ts:167-171`), so the user sees success while emails may be missing.

contracts.action: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees updates the external calendar event with the new attendee list
contracts.equivalent_path: Other callers of updateCalendarAttendees are the seated-booking flows (`createNewSeat.ts:147`, `attendeeRescheduleSeatedBooking.ts:39,92`).
contracts.before_after: It returns early with only a console.error when `booking.references` is empty (`EventManager.ts:597-600`). Otherwise it calls updateAllCalendarEvents, which falls back to loading the credential from the DB when the acting user lacks it (`EventManager.ts:845-870`). The handler ignores the return value.
contracts.visible_effect: The organizer's calendar event gets the new attendees, if a calendar reference exists.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing calendar reference or an update failure is invisible to the user: the handler still returns success and sends the emails.

summary: The PR adds an "Add guests" action: a dialog, a `bookings.addGuests` tRPC mutation, two email templates and a `MultiEmail` UI component. The main problems are in the handler. The team admin check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so only owners pass and admins are refused. The blacklist comparison does not lowercase the guest, so case variants get through. The server does not dedupe guests. Attendees are written to the DB before the calendar and email steps, so a failure there leaves the guests saved but the user sees an error and cannot retry. `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores the event type's host and attendee email-disable settings, which the sibling location-change function honours. In the dialog, the invalid-email banner persists after a successful add, and the error fallback toast is dead code. `MultiEmail` duplicates the form-builder version and imports its own package barrel. There are no tests."
